- Functionality for rounding or truncating a `DateTime`by a`TimeDelta`.
- [serde](https://docs.rs/serde/index.html)- `serde`
- Serialization/Deserialization with serde

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Date](https://docs.rs/struct.Date.html)- Deprecated
- ISO 8601 calendar date with time zone.
- [Date](https://docs.rs/struct.DateTime.html)- Time
- ISO 8601 combined date and time with time zone.
- [Days](https://docs.rs/struct.Days.html)
- A duration in calendar days.
- [Fixed](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedOffset.html)- Offset
- The time zone with fixed offset, from UTC-23:59:59 to UTC+23:59:59.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.Local.html)- `clock`
- The local timescale.
- [Months](https://docs.rs/struct.Months.html)
- A duration in calendar months
- [Naive](https://docs.rs/struct.NaiveDate.html)- Date
- ISO 8601 calendar date without timezone.
Allows for every [proleptic Gregorian date](https://docs.rs/struct.NaiveDate.html#calendar-date)from Jan 1, 262145 BCE to Dec 31, 262143 CE. Also supports the conversion from ISO 8601 ordinal and week date.
- [Naive](https://docs.rs/struct.NaiveDateTime.html)- Date - Time
- ISO 8601 combined date and time without timezone.
- [Naive](https://docs.rs/struct.NaiveTime.html)- Time
- ISO 8601 time without timezone. Allows for the nanosecond precision and optional leap second representation.
- [OutOf](https://docs.rs/struct.OutOfRange.html)- Range
- Out of range error type used in various converting APIs
- [Time](https://docs.rs/struct.TimeDelta.html)- Delta
- Time duration with nanosecond precision.
- [Utc](https://docs.rs/struct.Utc.html)
- The UTC time zone. This is the most efficient time zone when you don’t need the local time. It is also used as an offset (which is also a dummy type).
- [Weekday](https://docs.rs/struct.WeekdaySet.html)- Set
- A collection of `Weekday`

# quick_xml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/quick-xml/^0.41/

## Expand description

High performance XML reader/writer.

[§](https://docs.rs#description)Description

quick-xml contains two modes of operation:

A streaming API based on the [StAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StAX) model. This is suited for larger XML documents which
cannot completely read into memory at once.

The user has to explicitly *ask* for the next XML event, similar to a database cursor.
This is achieved by the following two structs:

- `Reader`
- `Writer`

Especially for nested XML elements, the user must keep track *where* (how deep)
in the XML document the current event is located.

quick-xml contains optional support of asynchronous reading and writing using [tokio](https://tokio.rs/).
To get it enable the [ async-tokio](https://docs.rs#async-tokio) feature.

Furthermore, quick-xml also contains optional [Serde](https://serde.rs/) support to directly
serialize and deserialize from structs, without having to deal with the XML events.
To get it enable the [ serialize](https://docs.rs#serialize) feature. Read more about mapping Rust types
to XML in the documentation of

[module. Also check](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)

`de`[module.](https://docs.rs/serde_helpers/index.html)

`serde_helpers`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`quick-xml` supports the following features:

-
`async-tokio``tokio`’s IO-Traits by enabling[reading events](https://docs.rs/reader/struct.Reader.html#method.read_event_into_async)from types implementing`tokio::io::AsyncBufRead`
-
`encoding`Currently, only ASCII-compatible encodings are supported. For example, UTF-16 will not work (therefore, `quick-xml`is not[standard compliant](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml11/#charencoding)).Thus, quick-xml supports all encodings of `encoding_rs`encodings you need to use the `DecodingReader`You should stop processing a document when one of these encodings is detected, if you do not use `DecodingReader`Because these are the only supported encodings that are not ASCII compatible, you can check for them: `use quick_xml::events::Event; use quick_xml::reader::Reader; let xml = to_utf16le_with_bom(r#"<?xml encoding='UTF-16'?><element/>"#); let mut reader = Reader::from_reader(xml.as_ref()); reader.config_mut().trim_text(true); let mut buf = Vec::new(); let mut unsupported = false; loop { if !reader.decoder().encoding().is_ascii_compatible() { unsupported = true; break; } buf.clear(); match reader.read_event_into(&mut buf).unwrap() { Event::Eof => break, _ => {} } } assert_eq!(unsupported, true);`
-
`escape-html`[HTML 5 entities](https://dev.w3.org/html5/html-author/charref)in`unescape`[https://html.spec.whatwg.org/entities.json](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/entities.json).
-
`overlapped-lists`When this feature is enabled, the XML: `<any-name> <item/> <another-item/> <item/> <item/> </any-name>`could be deserialized to a struct: `#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")] struct AnyName { item: Vec<()>, another_item: (), }`When this feature is not enabled (default), only the first element will be associated with the field, and the deserialized type will report an error (duplicated field) when the deserializer encounters a second `<item/>`.Note, that enabling this feature can lead to high and even unlimited memory consumption, because deserializer needs to check all events up to the end of a container tag ( `</any-name>`in this example) to figure out that there are no more items for a field. If`</any-name>`or even EOF is not encountered, the parsing will never end which can lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) scenario.Having several lists and overlapped elements for them in XML could also lead to quadratic parsing time, because the deserializer must check the list of events as many times as the number of sequence fields present in the schema. To reduce negative consequences, always [limit](https://docs.rs/de/struct.Deserializer.html#method.event_buffer_size)the maximum number of events that`Deserializer`This feature works only with `serialize`feature and has no effect if`serialize`is not enabled.
-
`serde-types``serde`This feature does NOT provide XML serializer or deserializer. You should use the `serialize`feature for that instead.
-
`serialize``serde`This feature does NOT enables serialization of the types inside quick-xml. If you need that, use the `serde-types`feature.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# aerocontext_planning - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/target-redirect/aerocontext_planning/

## Expand description

Flight-route planning: the single engine that turns a route or a flight plan into usable geometry.

Every frontend — the `aerocontext` CLI, the MCP `route_brief` tool, a
future GUI or iOS app — composes this crate rather than reimplementing
any of it. The hub is the [ flightplan::FlightPlan](https://docs.rs/flightplan/struct.FlightPlan.html) domain model;
Garmin

`.fpl` is one *codec*(inside

[), not the privileged format, so other formats slot in beside it without touching planning logic.](https://docs.rs/flightplan/index.html)

`flightplan`The pieces:

- `flightplan`- `FlightPlan`model and its- `.fpl`codec.
- `route`- `NavDataSnapshot`
- `corridor`
- `crosssection`- `AircraftProfile`

This crate consumes the cycle-stamped snapshot that `aerocontext-navdata`
produces; it never fetches or distributes data itself.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use corridor::`- [Corridor](https://docs.rs/corridor/struct.Corridor.html);
- `pub use corridor::`- [CorridorError](https://docs.rs/corridor/enum.CorridorError.html);
- `pub use crosssection::`- [CrossSection](https://docs.rs/crosssection/struct.CrossSection.html);
- `pub use crosssection::`- [CrossSectionError](https://docs.rs/crosssection/enum.CrossSectionError.html);
- `pub use crosssection::`- [CrossSectionSample](https://docs.rs/crosssection/struct.CrossSectionSample.html);
- `pub use crosssection::`- [FlightPhase](https://docs.rs/crosssection/enum.FlightPhase.html);
- `pub use flightplan::`- [FlightPlan](https://docs.rs/flightplan/struct.FlightPlan.html);
- `pub use flightplan::`- [FplError](https://docs.rs/flightplan/enum.FplError.html);
- `pub use flightplan::`- [PlanWaypoint](https://docs.rs/flightplan/struct.PlanWaypoint.html);
- `pub use flightplan::`- [WaypointType](https://docs.rs/flightplan/enum.WaypointType.html);
- `pub use route::`- [ExpandedRoute](https://docs.rs/route/struct.ExpandedRoute.html);
- `pub use route::`- [RouteError](https://docs.rs/route/enum.RouteError.html);
- `pub use route::`- [RoutePoint](https://docs.rs/route/struct.RoutePoint.html);

- `pub use route::`- [expand_str](https://docs.rs/route/fn.expand_str.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [corridor](https://docs.rs/corridor/index.html)
- Route corridors: a buffered polygon around a centerline, plus the leg-wise spatial predicates weather/TFR/NOTAM association uses.
- [crosssection](https://docs.rs/crosssection/index.html)
- The route cross-section: the vertical profile along a flight plan — where it climbs, cruises, and descends, and the estimated time and altitude at each waypoint.
- [flightplan](https://docs.rs/flightplan/index.html)
- Garmin FlightPlan v1 `.fpl`flight plans: import, export, and the bridge to a`aerocontext_core::RouteBriefingRequest`
- [route](https://docs.rs/route/index.html)
- Flight-plan route strings: tokenize, then expand against a
`NavDataSnapshot`

# aerocontext_planning/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Flight-route planning: the single engine that turns a route or a
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! flight plan into usable geometry.
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//!
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! Every frontend — the `aerocontext` CLI, the MCP `route_brief` tool, a
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! future GUI or iOS app — composes this crate rather than reimplementing
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! any of it. The hub is the [`flightplan::FlightPlan`] domain model;
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! Garmin `.fpl` is one *codec* (inside [`flightplan`]), not the
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! privileged format, so other formats slot in beside it without
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! touching planning logic.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! The pieces:
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! - [`flightplan`] — the `FlightPlan` model and its `.fpl` codec.
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! - [`route`] — expand a route (idents, airways, DCT, lat/lon, SID/STAR
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!   tokens) against a [`NavDataSnapshot`](aerocontext_core::NavDataSnapshot)
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!   into ordered geometry.
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! - [`corridor`] — a width-bounded corridor around a route, with
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!   leg-wise spatial association.
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! - [`crosssection`] — the vertical profile (climb/cruise/descent, time
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!   en route, fuel) from an
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!   [`AircraftProfile`](aerocontext_core::AircraftProfile).
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! This crate consumes the cycle-stamped snapshot that `aerocontext-navdata`
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! produces; it never fetches or distributes data itself.
[24](https://docs.rs#24)
[25](https://docs.rs#25)pub mod corridor;
[26](https://docs.rs#26)pub mod crosssection;
[27](https://docs.rs#27)pub mod flightplan;
[28](https://docs.rs#28)pub mod route;
[29](https://docs.rs#29)
[30](https://docs.rs#30)pub use corridor::{Corridor, CorridorError};
[31](https://docs.rs#31)pub use crosssection::{CrossSection, CrossSectionError, CrossSectionSample, FlightPhase};
[32](https://docs.rs#32)pub use flightplan::{FlightPlan, FplError, PlanWaypoint, WaypointType};
[33](https://docs.rs#33)pub use route::{ExpandedRoute, RouteError, RoutePoint, RouteToken, expand_str};

# aerocontext_planning::flightplan - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/aerocontext_planning/flightplan/index.html

## Expand description

Garmin FlightPlan v1 `.fpl` flight plans: import, export, and the
bridge to a [ aerocontext_core::RouteBriefingRequest](https://docs.rs/aerocontext-core/0.4.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aerocontext_core/route_request/struct.RouteBriefingRequest.html).

The schema is Garmin’s `http://www8.garmin.com/xmlschemas/FlightPlan/v1`:
a `<waypoint-table>` dictionary of `<waypoint>` entries (identifier,
type, lat, lon) and an ordered `<route>` of `<route-point>`s that
reference it. ForeFlight and other tools add a `<flight-data>` block
(ETD, cruise altitude) and an `<aircraft>` block as siblings; those are
preserved on import and re-emitted on export. Parsing is lenient —
`country-code`/`comment` (strictly required by the XSD) are treated as
optional, since real exporters omit them — but a route point that does
not resolve to a table waypoint is a hard error: a corridor must never
be built from a hole.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Flight](https://docs.rs/struct.FlightPlan.html)- Plan
- An imported Garmin flight plan: ordered route plus the metadata other tools attach.
- [Plan](https://docs.rs/struct.PlanWaypoint.html)- Waypoint
- One ordered waypoint of an imported plan: its identifier, type, and
position (carried by the `.fpl`itself, so no snapshot is needed to build geometry).

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [FplError](https://docs.rs/enum.FplError.html)
- Failure parsing a Garmin `.fpl`document.
- [Waypoint](https://docs.rs/enum.WaypointType.html)- Type
- A Garmin waypoint type. Recognized values round-trip on export;
an unknown type is coerced to `USER WAYPOINT`.

---

# aerocontext_planning::route - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/aerocontext_planning/route/index.html

## Expand description

Flight-plan route strings: tokenize, then expand against a
[ NavDataSnapshot](https://docs.rs/aerocontext-core/0.4.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aerocontext_core/navdata/struct.NavDataSnapshot.html) into an ordered
point list.

v0.1 scope: idents (airports/navaids/fixes), airways (`V`/`J`/`T`/`Q`
and the other published designator families), `DCT`, lat/lon waypoints
(`45N073W`, `4530N07315W`), and SID/STAR procedure tokens — the latter
are recognized and reported but contribute no geometry (no procedure
engine). Anything else fails loudly with a typed error: a corridor
must never silently omit legs.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Expanded](https://docs.rs/struct.ExpandedRoute.html)- Route
- An expanded route: geometry plus the procedures awaiting a future procedure engine.
- [Route](https://docs.rs/struct.RoutePoint.html)- Point
- A route point produced by expansion.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteError.html)- Error
- Failure parsing or expanding a route string.
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteToken.html)- Token
- One token of a route string.
- [Unsupported](https://docs.rs/enum.UnsupportedKind.html)- Kind
- What an unsupported token is.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [expand](https://docs.rs/fn.expand.html)
- Expand tokens into ordered geometry.
- [expand_](https://docs.rs/fn.expand_str.html)- str
- Parse and expand in one step.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Tokenize a route string. Fails on the first unsupported token — a corridor must never silently omit legs.

---

# aerocontext_planning::corridor - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/aerocontext_planning/corridor/index.html

## Expand description

Route corridors: a buffered polygon around a centerline, plus the leg-wise spatial predicates weather/TFR/NOTAM association uses.

The display polygon is built by offsetting each centerline vertex
perpendicular to the local bearing (miter-clamped joins, semicircular
end caps). Spatial truth is deliberately **leg-wise**, not
polygon-wise: [ Corridor::contains](https://docs.rs/struct.Corridor.html#method.contains) and

[evaluate cross-track/along- track per leg, which stays correct even where a hairpin makes the display ring self-intersect.](https://docs.rs/struct.Corridor.html#method.distance_to_centerline_nm)

`Corridor::distance_to_centerline_nm`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Corridor](https://docs.rs/struct.Corridor.html)
- A buffered route corridor.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Corridor](https://docs.rs/enum.CorridorError.html)- Error
- Failure constructing a corridor.

---

# aerocontext_planning::crosssection - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/aerocontext_planning/crosssection/index.html

## Expand description

The route cross-section: the vertical profile along a flight plan — where it climbs, cruises, and descends, and the estimated time and altitude at each waypoint.

This is what a “profile view” shows and what tells a briefing *which*
forecast hour and *which* altitudes to ask about along the route. It is
a no-wind, straight-line estimate from the operator’s
[ aerocontext_core::AircraftProfile](https://docs.rs/aerocontext-core/0.4.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aerocontext_core/aircraft/struct.AircraftProfile.html) —

**advisory**, not a performance computation.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Cross](https://docs.rs/struct.CrossSection.html)- Section
- The vertical profile of a route plus its trip totals.
- [Cross](https://docs.rs/struct.CrossSectionSample.html)- Section - Sample
- One sampled point of the vertical profile.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Cross](https://docs.rs/enum.CrossSectionError.html)- Section - Error
- Failure building a cross-section.
- [Flight](https://docs.rs/enum.FlightPhase.html)- Phase
- Flight phase at a point along the route.

---

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aerocontext_core/aircraft.rs.html#76-87)#### pub fn [validate](https://docs.rs#method.validate)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [ProfileError](https://docs.rs/enum.ProfileError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aerocontext_core/aircraft.rs.html#76-87)

#### pub fn [validate](https://docs.rs#method.validate)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [ProfileError](https://docs.rs/enum.ProfileError.html)>

Validate the profile for the advisory performance math: every figure finite, speeds and rates strictly positive, fuel figures non-negative, and the reserve within a sane bound. Returns the first failure.

The cross-section builder calls this, so an out-of-range profile yields a typed error instead of a non-finite estimate or a panicking duration conversion.

Build the cross-section for `plan` flown per `profile`. Cruise
altitude comes from the plan; departure and destination are taken
at sea level (field elevations are not in the `.fpl`), so the
climb and descent ramps are conservative.

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/aerocontext_planning/flightplan/enum.FplError.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum FplError {
    Xml(
```
[Error](https://docs.rs/quick-xml/0.41.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quick_xml/errors/enum.Error.html)),
    Encoding([EncodingError](https://docs.rs/quick-xml/0.41.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quick_xml/encoding/enum.EncodingError.html)),
    IncompleteWaypoint {
        identifier: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
        field: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    },
    BadCoordinate {
        identifier: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
        field: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
        value: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    },
    UnknownRoutePoint {
        identifier: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    },
    EmptyRoute,
}## Expand description

Failure parsing a Garmin `.fpl` document.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Xml)

### Xml([Error](https://docs.rs/quick-xml/0.41.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quick_xml/errors/enum.Error.html))

The bytes were not valid XML.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Encoding)

### Encoding([EncodingError](https://docs.rs/quick-xml/0.41.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/quick_xml/encoding/enum.EncodingError.html))

A text node could not be decoded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IncompleteWaypoint)

### IncompleteWaypoint

A waypoint-table entry was missing a required field.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BadCoordinate)

### BadCoordinate

A `<lat>`/`<lon>` value did not parse as a coordinate.

#### Fields

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnknownRoutePoint)

### UnknownRoutePoint

A route point referenced an identifier absent from the waypoint table; a corridor must never be built from a hole.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmptyRoute)

### EmptyRoute

The document carried no route points.

# WaypointType in aerocontext_planning::flightplan - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aerocontext-planning/0.4.5/aerocontext_planning/flightplan/enum.WaypointType.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum WaypointType {
    Airport,
    Ndb,
    Vor,
    Int,
    IntVrp,
    User,
}
```
## Expand description

A Garmin waypoint type. Recognized values round-trip on export;
an unknown type is coerced to `USER WAYPOINT`.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Airport)

### Airport

`AIRPORT`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Ndb)

### Ndb

`NDB`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vor)

### Vor

`VOR`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Int)

### Int

`INT` (enroute intersection / fix).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.IntVrp)

### IntVrp

`INT-VRP` (visual reporting point).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.User)

### User

`USER WAYPOINT` (operator-defined lat/lon).
